question: How does each of the five define and report advisor headcount -- and what does each definition include or exclude?

claims.text: The firms define advisor headcount differently, so their figures are not compared or combined. Merrill (Bank of America) defines 'Total wealth advisors' at period end as including advisors across all wealth management businesses in GWIM and Consumer Banking.

Raymond James Financial reports financial advisor headcount as 'Total advisors,' the sum of two categories: 'Employees' (employee financial advisors) and 'Independent contractors' (independent advisors).

Raymond James Financial excludes financial advisors associated with firms in its RCS (RIA & Custody Services) division from its financial advisor counts, although their client assets are included in AUA.
Raymond James Financial states that advisors in its RCS division are not included in its financial advisor metric, although their client assets are included in PCG AUA.
As of September 30, 2025, Raymond James Financial reports approximately 19,500 associates (including 3,878 employee financial advisors) and 5,065 independent advisors.

The firms define advisor headcount differently, so their figures are not compared or combined. Morgan Stanley reported 15,950 Wealth Management representatives for the quarter ended December 31, 2020, its advisor headcount figure. Why it might matter: the source does not say.
Morgan Stanley reported 15,469 Wealth Management representatives for the quarter ended September 30, 2020.
Morgan Stanley reported 15,468 Wealth Management representatives for the quarter ended December 31, 2019.

The firms define advisor headcount differently, so their figures are not compared or combined. The Partnership reported 20,425 financial advisors (actual) at year end 2025. Why it might matter: the source does not say.
The Partnership reported 20,125 financial advisors (actual) at year end 2024.
The Partnership reported 19,232 financial advisors (actual) at year end 2023.
The Partnership reported an average of 20,331 financial advisors for the year 2025, 19,650 for the year 2024, and 18,945 for the year 2023 (the source does not state the periods in a usable form).
The Partnership reported 20,429 financial advisors at period end September 26, 2025, and an average of 20,368 for the third quarter of 2025.
The Partnership reported 20,550 financial advisors at period end March 27, 2026, and an average of 20,506 for the first quarter of 2026.
The Partnership reported 20,514 financial advisors at period end June 26, 2026, and an average of 20,537 for the second quarter of 2026.
The Partnership reported 20,309 financial advisors at period end June 27, 2025, and an average of 20,316 for the second quarter of 2025.
The Partnership stated its more than 20,000 financial advisors serve more than 9 million clients as of June 26, 2026. Why it might matter: the source does not say.

The firms define advisor headcount differently, so their figures are not compared or combined. Bank of America reports 'Total wealth advisors' at period end of 18,916 at December 31, 2023, defined as including advisors across all wealth management businesses in GWIM and Consumer Banking.
Bank of America reports 'Total wealth advisors' at period end of 19,273 at December 31, 2022.
Bank of America reports 'Total wealth advisors' at period end of 19,130 at September 30, 2023, 19,099 at June 30, 2023, and 19,243 at March 31, 2023.
Bank of America's investor day materials report more than 15,000 wealth advisors for Merrill and Private Bank combined.

The firms define advisor headcount differently, so their figures are not compared or combined. Raymond James Financial reported 8,943 total financial advisors as of September 30, 2025, 8,787 as of September 30, 2024, and 8,712 as of September 30, 2023 (the source does not state the periods in a usable form). Why it might matter: the source does not say.
Raymond James Financial reported 3,878 employee financial advisors as of September 30, 2025, 3,826 as of September 30, 2024, and 3,693 as of September 30, 2023.
Raymond James Financial reported 5,065 independent contractor financial advisors as of September 30, 2025, 4,961 as of September 30, 2024, and 5,019 as of September 30, 2023.
Raymond James Financial's advisor count comprises employee financial advisors and independent contractor financial advisors, and excludes financial advisors associated with firms in its RCS division.

The firms define advisor headcount differently, so their figures are not compared or combined. Schwab states that growth in its headcount includes growth in financial consultants and wealth advisors, which it attributes to supporting its expanding client base.
Schwab states that higher compensation and benefits expense reflected growth in headcount, including financial consultants and wealth advisors.
Schwab describes its investor-facing advisory roles as Financial Consultants, Active Trader Financial Consultants, and Wealth Consultants, who provide guidance and relationship management.
Schwab states it is continuing to hire financial consultants and wealth advisers while expanding its branch footprint.

The firms define advisor headcount differently, so their figures are not compared or combined. Merrill (Bank of America) reports 'Total wealth advisors' at period end, which includes advisors across all wealth management businesses in GWIM and Consumer Banking; at December 31, 2023 the figure was 18,916.

The firms define advisor headcount differently, so their figures are not compared or combined. Raymond James Financial reports its financial advisor headcount as the sum of employee financial advisors and independent contractor financial advisors, shown as 'Total advisors' of 8,943 as of September 30, 2025.
As of September 30, 2025, Raymond James Financial had approximately 19,500 associates (including 3,878 employee financial advisors) and 5,065 independent advisors.

Raymond James Financial states that advisors in its RCS division are not included in its financial advisor metric, although their client assets are included in PCG AUA.

The firms define advisor headcount differently, so their figures are not compared or combined. Morgan Stanley disclosed 'Wealth Management representatives' of 15,950 as of December 31, 2020 in its Wealth Management Metrics (Advisor-led channel), which is its financial advisor headcount metric.
Morgan Stanley disclosed 'Wealth Management representatives' of 15,469 as of September 30, 2020, and 15,468 as of December 31, 2019, in its Wealth Management Metrics.

The firms define advisor headcount differently, so their figures are not compared or combined. Schwab's filings attribute compensation and benefits expense growth to growth in headcount, including growth in financial consultants and wealth advisors, without disclosing a specific advisor headcount figure.
Schwab describes its advisor/relationship roles: Financial Consultants, Active Trader Financial Consultants, and Wealth Consultants provide guidance, relationship management, and specialized support.
Schwab's ADV Part 1A filing reports 30,690 employees, defined as including full- and part-time employees but excluding clerical workers.

Schwab's ADV Part 1A filing reports that 4,127 of its employees perform investment advisory functions (including research), and 6,584 are registered with one or more state securities authorities as investment adviser representatives.

The firms define advisor headcount differently, so their figures are not compared or combined. Edward Jones reports financial advisor headcount under the metric label 'Financial advisors (actual),' disclosing both the count at period end and the average for the period; at year end 2025 the Partnership reported 20,425 financial advisors.
The Partnership also reports the average number of financial advisors for the period; the average for 2025 was 20,331.
The Partnership reports financial advisor headcount by geographic segment; at year end 2025 the U.S. segment had 19,540 financial advisors and the Canada segment had 885.

The Partnership discloses financial advisor headcount as 'Financial advisors (actual),' reported 'At period end' and 'Average' and split between U.S. and Canada segments; the parenthetical '(actual)' indicates advisors are counted as actual individuals rather than on a full-time equivalent basis.

The firms define advisor headcount differently, so their figures are not compared or combined. Bank of America's Global Wealth & Investment Management Key Indicators report advisor headcount as 'Total wealth advisors' at period end, a metric defined as including advisors across all wealth management businesses in GWIM and Consumer Banking.
Total wealth advisors at period end were 18,916 at December 31, 2023, and 19,273 at December 31, 2022.
The 2025 Investor Day deck describes Merrill and the Private Bank as having an industry-leading advisor force of wealth advisors.

The firms define advisor headcount differently, so their figures are not compared or combined. Raymond James Financial reports advisor headcount as 'Financial advisors,' broken into 'Employees' (employee financial advisors) and 'Independent contractors,' with a 'Total advisors' line, as of each September 30.
Raymond James Financial reported 8,943 total financial advisors as of September 30, 2025, 8,787 as of September 30, 2024, and 8,712 as of September 30, 2023.
As of September 30, 2025, Raymond James Financial reported 3,878 employee financial advisors and 5,065 independent contractor advisors.
As of September 30, 2025, Raymond James Financial had approximately 19,500 associates, including 3,878 employee financial advisors, and 5,065 independent advisors.
